comment: How many different strings a type="regex" pattern can make, as `uniq="true"` counts it before drawing. A class counts its distinct characters, a sequence multiplies, an alternation adds, {m,n} adds every length it allows, a back-reference counts once and a conditional counts both branches. `advanced` counts advanced_regex patterns the same way: a weighted choice adds its branches, and its conditional adds one more for a row that matches no branch unless a * branch catches it. Exact for literals, classes and repeats; an upper bound otherwise. Saturates at 9007199254740991 (2^53 − 1). Regenerate with: npm run regex:space -- --update

patterns.why: a plate number: 26² · 10⁴ · 10²
the smallest honest space: one hundred
a variable length adds EVERY length it allows: 10² + 10³
nine lengths, eleven billion strings
a literal is one string
an alternation adds its branches
OVERCOUNTED — reaches abc two ways, so four is counted for three strings
a class counts DISTINCT characters, not how often one is written
a back-reference repeats a group already counted: two, not four
the same by name
OVERCOUNTED — a conditional counts both branches, though a row takes one
an optional is a repeat of zero or one
zero repeats is the empty string, once
a repeated literal stays one string
the dot is the 95 printable ASCII characters
a shorthand class
letters, digits and the underscore
a negated class is printable ASCII less what it names
the empty string counts too: 1 + 63 + 63²
OVERCOUNTED — two branches, one string: the case the draw has to catch
10¹⁵ — still exact
10¹⁶ is past 2^53 − 1, so it saturates there
saturates part-way through the sum

advanced.why: a weighted choice adds its branches: (1 + 1) · 10³
a weighted choice inside a repeat: 2² · 10
a weighted choice under an alternation: (1 + 2) · 10²
a conditional with no * adds one for the row that matches nothing: 2 · (2 + 1)
with a * branch nothing falls through: 2 · (2 + 1)
OVERCOUNTED — both branches count although a row takes one: 2 · 7 · 10
OVERCOUNTED — the case the draw has to catch
no weighted choice at all: the same count as a plain pattern
saturates at 2^53 − 1 like a plain pattern
